nodes.What it is: A robot cannot read its true position directly; it maintains a belief about possible states. Probability distributions and covariance describe both the best guess and how uncertain it is.
nodes.Prerequisites: Python, vectors, basic probability; distinguish state from measurement.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Bayes filtering remains the foundation beneath modern estimators. Correct uncertainty and correlated measurements matter as much as a smooth-looking trajectory. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Groningen robotics course; PythonRobotics contributors; Springer SLAM authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small noisy-position simulation runs on a laptop and needs no robotics hardware.

nodes.What it is: Dead reckoning estimates motion by adding up wheel rotations or inertial measurements over time. Small wheel-slip or sensor-bias errors accumulate, so this is a short-term reference rather than a permanent global position.
nodes.Prerequisites: Planar coordinate transforms, velocity integration, timestamps; basic sensor noise.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Modern Robotics explains the wheel-to-chassis integration used in practical mobile bases. Contemporary fusion still needs explicit bias and wheel-slip tests; inertial integration alone does not stop drift. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Lynch and Park; ROBOTIS; robot_localization maintainers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Synthetic wheel traces give a first demo before touching motors or buying a base.

nodes.What it is: A Kalman filter alternates motion predictions with sensor corrections, weighting each by uncertainty. EKF linearizes nonlinear models, while UKF propagates selected sample points through them.
nodes.Prerequisites: Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty; Jacobians, covariance; wheel/inertial motion models.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ROS robot_localization exposes EKF and UKF with configurable sensor inputs and timeouts. Reliable fusion needs consistent frames, realistic covariance and avoidance of double-counted data; a filter does not create absolute information. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Charles River Analytics / robot_localization community; GTSAM; Groningen
nodes._accessibility_reason: Existing packages reduce implementation work, but tuning covariance and diagnosing frames takes mathematical care.

nodes.What it is: A particle filter represents possible robot poses as many weighted guesses. Unlike a single Gaussian, it can keep several plausible locations in a repeated corridor and recover after being moved unexpectedly.
nodes.Prerequisites: Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty; sampling, sensor likelihoods, occupancy maps.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Particle methods remain useful when localization beliefs have multiple peaks. Their cost grows with state dimension, and global recovery must be tested separately from easy tracking near a known start. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: 2D landmark simulations are easy to animate; designing informative likelihoods and resampling needs some probability.

nodes.What it is: A factor graph connects unknown poses to noisy constraints such as odometry or landmark observations. Solving the graph adjusts a whole trajectory together instead of only correcting the newest pose.
nodes.Prerequisites: Least squares, Jacobians, rigid transforms, covariance; Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: GTSAM supports factor-graph inference and IMU preintegration. RSS 2025 includes certifiable optimization work, but offline bundle-adjustment guarantees do not imply every real-time SLAM graph is globally solved. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Frank Dellaert / Borglab; Georgia Tech; MIT SPARK; Harvard computational robotics researchers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Python bindings make tiny graphs accessible; gauge freedom and nonlinear optimization are the main learning cost.

nodes.What it is: An estimator needs to know where sensors sit and when each measurement was taken. Observability asks which quantities the available motion and measurements can actually determine, such as whether absolute yaw or scale is knowable.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms, camera geometry, Jacobians, Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr solves camera/IMU spatial and temporal calibration; OpenVINS supports online calibration components. LaMAria shows that calibration can vary over long sessions; good residuals alone do not prove all parameters are identifiable. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH Zurich ASL; OpenVINS / Patrick Geneva and collaborators; ETH CVG
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public bags avoid hardware work, but selecting excitation, interpreting uncertainty and handling clocks is demanding.

nodes.What it is: Visual odometry tracks camera motion through images; adding an IMU helps through fast motion and short visual gaps. SLAM additionally reuses places and maps to correct accumulated drift, which plain odometry does not do.
nodes.Prerequisites: Camera geometry; Estimator calibration, timing & observability; filtering or factor graphs.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ORB-SLAM3 supplies visual/inertial multi-map SLAM and OpenVINS a filter-based VIO baseline. LaMAria 2025 highlights city-scale failures; monocular-only metric scale and inertial initialization need explicit treatment. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: University of Zaragoza SLAMLab; OpenVINS; ETH CVG
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public EuRoC/TUM-VI examples are software-first, although C++ dependencies and initialization are real obstacles.

nodes.What it is: A planar laser measures distances around a mobile robot; matching scans estimates its motion. An occupancy grid records which floor-plan cells appear free or blocked, while graph optimization keeps repeated visits aligned.
nodes.Prerequisites: Wheel & inertial dead reckoning; occupancy probabilities, ROS messages and transforms.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SLAM Toolbox documents ROS 2 mapping, graph serialization, localization and lifelong-map workflows. A flat laser map is a useful baseline, not a complete representation of stairs, overhangs or moving people. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Steve Macenski; ROS 2 navigation community; ROBOTIS
nodes._accessibility_reason: A recorded laser scan bag produces a recognizable floor plan without new hardware.

nodes.What it is: A 3D lidar records clouds of surface points, which can be aligned to estimate motion. IMU fusion helps undo motion during a scan and bridge weak geometry; global loop closure is a separate component.
nodes.Prerequisites: Point-cloud registration, SE(3), inertial bias, calibration; filtering and factor graphs.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: KISS-ICP is a simple lidar-only odometry reference, FAST-LIO2 a filter-based LIO reference, and LIO-SAM a smoothing-based alternative. FAST-LIVO2 released code in 2025 for lidar/IMU/camera fusion; more sensors bring synchronization and compute risks. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: University of Bonn; HKU MARS; Tixiao Shan and collaborators
nodes._accessibility_reason: Datasets remove purchase barriers, but point formats, deskewing and ROS 1-era dependencies require substantial debugging.

nodes.What it is: Place recognition proposes that a robot has returned somewhere familiar. Geometric verification checks that guess before adding a loop constraint; relocalization recovers a pose after tracking was lost.
nodes.Prerequisites: Visual or lidar odometry; Factor graphs, smoothing & pose-graph SLAM; feature matching.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ORB-SLAM3 and RTAB-Map provide practical map-reuse and loop-closure references. Learned matching priors such as MASt3R broaden experiments, but look-alike scenes still demand geometric checks and false-positive reporting. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: University of Zaragoza; IntRoLab; NAVER LABS
nodes._accessibility_reason: Image sequences and graph visualizations suit software students, with no need to construct a moving robot.

nodes.What it is: People, moved furniture and changing lighting can make old map assumptions wrong. Robust estimation rejects bad constraints and tracks when a map or pose is no longer trustworthy instead of silently reporting success.
nodes.Prerequisites: Place recognition, loop closure & relocalization; Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; failure metrics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DynaSLAM is an older dynamic-scene teaching baseline, not a 2026 leaderboard winner. SLAM Toolbox supports persistent mapping and LaMAria exposes long-session challenges; dependable recovery and map-version policies remain important research questions. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: IntRoLab; SLAM Toolbox maintainers; ETH CVG; Zaragoza dynamic-SLAM researchers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Controlled dataset corruptions are cheap, but credible claims require failure detection, repeats and changing scenes.

nodes.What it is: A dense map models surfaces throughout a scene instead of only a sparse set of landmarks. Semantic labels add meaning, while neural priors and Gaussian splats can create detailed reconstructions; visual realism alone does not establish metric accuracy.
nodes.Prerequisites: Visual odometry & visual-inertial SLAM; GPU programming basics; map representations and evaluation.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SplaTAM (CVPR 2024) uses RGB-D Gaussian maps, MASt3R-SLAM (CVPR 2025) uses learned reconstruction priors, and PINGS (RSS 2025) couples radiance and distance fields. Hardware speed, monocular scale, dynamic objects and noncommercial prior licenses must be checked before deployment. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Imperial Dyson Robotics Lab; NAVER LABS; SplaTAM authors; Bonn/PRBonn; MIT SPARK
nodes._accessibility_reason: AI skills transfer well and public videos are enough, but GPU availability and geometry evaluation lower accessibility.

nodes.What it is: Several robots can combine partial maps if they discover which places they share and align their coordinate frames. Distributed methods exchange information without assuming every sensor stream can reach one central computer.
nodes.Prerequisites: Factor graphs, smoothing & pose-graph SLAM; loop verification; networking and distributed systems.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Kimera-Multi documents peer-to-peer robust mapping with inter-robot loop closures. Its ROS Noetic-era build is a reproducibility risk; network dropout, duplicate evidence and incorrect cross-robot matches need explicit tests. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT SPARK / Luca Carlone; Kimera-Multi collaborators
nodes._accessibility_reason: Multiple recorded sessions avoid buying a fleet, but map alignment, networking and old dependencies are substantial integration work.

nodes.What it is: Evaluation compares estimated trajectories with an independent reference and records when tracking fails. Absolute and relative errors answer different questions; alignment, time association and uncertainty calibration can otherwise hide mistakes.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic statistics, coordinate transforms; Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: evo and TUM provide established trajectory tools; LaMAria and the RSS 2025 workshop motivate long-session and failure-aware tests beyond one average ATE. Report runtime, tracking coverage and alignment rules as well as accuracy. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Michael Grupp; TUM CVG; ETH CVG; RSS visual-SLAM workshop organizers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Small trajectory files and plotting scripts deliver useful results on an ordinary laptop.

nodes.What it is: A legged robot can estimate its body motion using an IMU plus joint kinematics and feet believed to be stationary. Invariant filters exploit rotation and translation structure, but a slipping foot is not a reliable fixed landmark.
nodes.Prerequisites: Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; Lie groups; forward kinematics and contact assumptions.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The contact-aided InEKF has an open implementation and RSS theory; GTSAM documentation includes 2026 proprioceptive-estimation material. Absolute position and gravity-axis yaw are not observable from contact/IMU alone; good filtering cannot remove that ambiguity. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Ross Hartley; University of Michigan; Barrau and Bonnabel; Borglab / Seoul National University
nodes._accessibility_reason: Replay examples need no biped purchase, but Lie-group reasoning and contact validation need mathematical effort.

nodes.What it is: GNSS gives an outdoor position reference that can limit dead-reckoning drift. Fusion must translate latitude and longitude into a consistent local frame and account for heading, antenna placement and unreliable fixes near buildings.
nodes.Prerequisites: Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; frames and covariances; geographic versus local coordinates.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: robot_localization navsat_transform documents GPS, IMU heading and odometry inputs, including ENU/UTM conventions. LIO-SAM accepts GPS constraints; neither system turns bad multipath fixes into guaranteed centimeter accuracy. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: robot_localization community; Charles River Analytics; LIO-SAM authors; Borglab
nodes._accessibility_reason: Synthetic GNSS and public logs allow software-first fusion; real outdoor accuracy requires careful hardware and reference data.

robots_models.Name: PythonRobotics
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Educational Python examples: EKF localization, particle/histogram filters, GPS/IMU bias fusion, grid mapping and ICP.
robots_models.Why it matters: Readable baselines for learning uncertainty before integrating a full robot stack.

robots_models.Name: robot_localization
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Charles River Analytics and ROS community
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: EKF/UKF nodes; configurable sensor timeouts and frames; navsat_transform for GNSS.
robots_models.Why it matters: A practical fusion baseline, not a map-building or loop-closure system.

robots_models.Name: GTSAM
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: C++ factor graphs with Python/MATLAB interfaces, IMU preintegration and navigation examples; pin stable release, not develop.
robots_models.Why it matters: Makes uncertainty-aware graph estimation and legged-estimation experiments reusable.

robots_models.Name: Kalibr
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): ETH Zurich Autonomous Systems Lab and contributors
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Multi-camera, camera/IMU spatial-temporal, multi-IMU and rolling-shutter calibration.
robots_models.Why it matters: Poor extrinsics or clocks can invalidate an otherwise good SLAM experiment; older ROS build instructions need isolation.

robots_models.Name: OpenVINS
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: MSCKF sliding-window visual-inertial EKF; calibration features; evaluation utilities including NEES.
robots_models.Why it matters: A filter-based comparison to optimization-based visual SLAM, with useful consistency checks.

robots_models.Name: ORB-SLAM3
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Monocular, stereo, RGB-D and inertial modes; fisheye/pinhole support; multi-map SLAM; GPLv3.
robots_models.Why it matters: Established geometry-based baseline for tracking loss, scale and loop-closure experiments.

robots_models.Name: SLAM Toolbox
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: ROS 2 planar laser graph SLAM, map serialization, localization and lifelong mapping; LGPLv2.1.
robots_models.Why it matters: The easiest high-impact floor-plan demo without moving into motion planning.

robots_models.Name: RTAB-Map
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Mathieu Labbe / IntRoLab, Universite de Sherbrooke
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: RGB-D, stereo and lidar graph SLAM; appearance-based loop detection and memory management.
robots_models.Why it matters: Connects understandable 3D mapping videos to practical map reuse and relocalization.

robots_models.Name: KISS-ICP
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): PRBonn / University of Bonn and contributors
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Point-to-point ICP lidar odometry; Python CLI and official ROS 2 wrapper; MIT license.
robots_models.Why it matters: A simple baseline that helps reveal when a complicated fusion pipeline is not adding value.

robots_models.Name: FAST-LIO2
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Direct lidar/IMU iterated-filter odometry and ikd-tree mapping; 2.0 update July 2021; GPLv2.
robots_models.Why it matters: Compare filtering against smoothing without claiming core odometry provides global loop closure.

robots_models.Name: LIO-SAM
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: GTSAM lidar/IMU smoothing; mapping/GPS and IMU-preintegration graphs; original ROS 1 plus ROS 2 branch.
robots_models.Why it matters: Useful reference for factor design, sensor conventions and outdoors georeferencing.

robots_models.Name: FAST-LIVO2
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Chunran Zheng / HKU MARS Lab and collaborators
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Direct lidar-inertial-visual fusion; synchronized handheld rig resources; January 2025 code release; GPLv2.
robots_models.Why it matters: A recent multisensor reference; hardware synchronization and sensor calibration are first-class requirements.

robots_models.Name: TurtleBot3
robots_models.Price / access: Open platform documentation; current complete kit price unknown. Budget physical-base projects provisionally at EUR500-5k, verify quote before buying.
robots_models.Key specs: Modular ROS educational wheeled platform; vendor documents ROS 2 and Gazebo workflows; variant-dependent hardware.
robots_models.Why it matters: A recognizable reference mobile base for an eventual real floor-plan demo, not a required purchase.

robots_models.Name: evo
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Python CLI/library for trajectory comparison, APE/RPE and alignment; TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS formats; GPLv3.
robots_models.Why it matters: A standard way to turn impressive maps into comparable trajectory measurements.

robots_models.Name: DynaSLAM
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Berta Bescos and University of Zaragoza collaborators
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Dynamic-scene monocular/stereo/RGB-D SLAM with background inpainting; 2018 paper; Python 2.7/old framework dependencies.
robots_models.Why it matters: An instructive historical baseline for masking moving objects, not an easy modern production install.

robots_models.Name: SplaTAM
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Nikhil Keetha, Jay Karhade and collaborators
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; supported CUDA GPU required by documented workflow. GPU ownership/rental cost unknown and excluded from hardware bands.
robots_models.Key specs: Dense RGB-D tracking/mapping with 3D Gaussians; CVPR 2024; CUDA/PyTorch environment; BSD-3 source.
robots_models.Why it matters: Visually compelling mapping where reconstruction quality must be separated from pose accuracy.

robots_models.Name: MASt3R-SLAM
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Riku Murai, Eric Dexheimer, Andrew Davison / Imperial College London
robots_models.Price / access: Research code/checkpoints publicly accessible; MASt3R dependency has CC BY-NC-SA noncommercial terms. Do not treat the full stack as unrestricted open source; GPU cost unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: CVPR 2025 monocular dense SLAM built on MASt3R reconstruction/matching priors; CUDA extensions and pretrained checkpoints.
robots_models.Why it matters: Low incremental sensor cost for dense reconstructions, but prior licensing and monocular scale require care.

robots_models.Name: MASt3R
robots_models.Price / access: Public research code and checkpoint instructions; noncommercial code terms and checkpoint-specific licenses must be checked; GPU compute extra.
robots_models.Key specs: ECCV 2024 pairwise learned image matching/3D reconstruction prior; not a VLA or control policy; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 code.
robots_models.Why it matters: A concrete AI model behind learning-assisted SLAM, rather than a claim that an image model alone localizes a robot.

robots_models.Name: Kimera-Multi
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: Peer-to-peer distributed metric-semantic SLAM with robust inter/intra-robot loop handling; documented ROS Noetic build.
robots_models.Why it matters: A reference for collaborative map fusion; start with recorded data rather than purchasing several robots.

robots_models.Name: invariant-ekf
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Ross Hartley and collaborators, University of Michigan
robots_models.Price / access: Free source; compute, data storage and integration time are additional.
robots_models.Key specs: C++ invariant filter with IMU propagation, known/estimated landmarks and contact/kinematic updates; BSD-3.
robots_models.Why it matters: Enables contact-aided body-state experiments while keeping walking-policy design outside this branch.
